subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Seawall Engineering: Defending Coastlines From Rising Seas
description: A quick win: understand Seawall Engineering: Defending Coastlines From Rising Seas.

hook.text: Jakarta is sinking 25 cm per year while sea levels rise. Indonesia is moving its capital rather than fighting the ocean.

buildup.text: Traditional seawalls reflect wave energy, scouring the seabed and undermining the wall. They solve one problem and create another.

discovery.text: Living shorelines use oyster reefs, mangroves, and marshes to absorb waves naturally. They grow stronger instead of degrading.

twist.text: Miami Beach is raising roads by two feet and installing 80 pumps. The city is literally elevating itself above rising water.

climax.text: The MOSE barrier in Venice uses 78 inflatable gates to block high tides. Activated in 2020, it protects the city from floods.

punchline.text: Build walls. Raise roads. Grow reefs. Or move the capital entirely.

quiz.question: Why are traditional seawalls problematic as a long-term coastal defense?
options: They attract marine organisms that weaken the wall's concrete over time
They reflect wave energy that scours the seabed and undermines the wall itself
They block sediment transport, causing beaches downstream to erode faster
